notes:
Six bullets, four steps. Bullet 2 is the MECHANIC, not a step: it explains that an Afflictor curses anyone who comes near unless they are silenced, and that a Mute silences anyone who touches it, therefore curse first and silence second. Bullets 3 and 4 are one continuous set of walking directions ending at the Afflictor, and bullet 5 is the walk back ending at the Mute, so each merges into the entity it leads to rather than becoming a routing rung of its own.

Neither Beadeaux step can carry evidence. What you gain there is a Curse and a Silence -- status effects, which no packet reports and which rule 2 explicitly excludes. The Cursepaper key item is granted by bullet 1 and is therefore step 1's evidence, not step 4's.

The page says to pick 'one of the sets of machines' and then gives directions to only the easiest set, so the two grid refs are the easiest set's and not the only ones. Both grids are on Beadeaux's LOWER map, which shares its grid letters with the upper one -- the addon has no map-layer concept, so (G-8) and (G-7) will also match the upper map. Recorded as given and flagged.

The Afflictor is not clicked at all: it curses on approach. It is still recorded as the step's target because that is the thing you must reach, and it is a real markable entity.

steps.note: there is nothing to click -- it curses you on approach, and only if you are not already silenced, which is why it must come before the Mute. This is the easiest of several sets of machines; the page gives directions to no other.
touch it while cursed; the Silence is the second impression on the Cursepaper. Back east from the Afflictor, then the first turn north. Lower map again.

Bullet 5's two clauses ('speak with him THEN trade him') are one visit to one NPC and are kept as one trade step -- wedging a talk rung in front of it would split a single marker in two for no gain.

The Item Reqs' 'Pea Soup or Emerald Soup' is a genuine OR and is modelled as items/items_alt. The trailing 'Zoning is required in order to repeat this quest' is a cooldown note, not a step. notes:
The last leg of the Mythic weapon series, and the page is written for someone who already knows the series. Three judgement calls.

START. The header says 'Balrahn, Nyzul Isle' and the walkthrough never mentions Balrahn at all -- he is a floor cutscene inside an instance, not a standing giver, and v1 duly marks him in zone 77 where nobody can walk up to him. Start is moved to the thing bullet 1 sends you to, the tombstone in Caedarva Mire, with the header string kept verbatim in raw.

NAMES. The page writes the tombstone in lower case and never gives it a grid, and writes the palace entrance as 'the Palace doors (Imperial Whitegate)'. Both are recorded as the page has them, because both are single definite objects you demonstrably click, but neither live entity name is verified and the parenthetical is NOT a zone -- 'Imperial Whitegate' resolves to nothing, while 'Aht Urhgan Whitegate' (which the page itself uses further down, for Ghanraam) resolves to 50. Steps 1 to 3 are held at medium for this.

'Naja' is the page's abbreviation. The index the addon already ships names her 'Naja Salaheem' in 31 giver rows, so that is what is written; the short form would never match a live entity.

ITEMS. The mythic weapon itself cannot be recorded: it is one of fifteen-odd named weapons and the page names none of them, only 'your statless Mythic'. items stays empty on steps 2 and 3 with items_partial set, which is the honest way to say there is a holding requirement no name can express. The header's Quest Reqs key item, the Serpentking Zahak relief shard, resolves and is put on step 1 even though the walkthrough never mentions it.

Bullet 4's sub-bullets are about starting the NEXT mythic and about the storage NPC Ghanraam. They belong to a different quest and are not steps here. There is no evidence anywhere in this quest -- nothing observable is handed out until the reward.

STAGE D. Two removals. The Serpentking Zahak relief shard is gone from step 1's items: the header calls it Quest Reqs and the draft's own note calls it 'what proves Forging a New Myth is done', which makes it a PREREQUISITE, already carried by gates.prev, and not something the walkthrough ever says you must be holding when you click the tombstone. If the previous quest consumes it, a holding requirement there would stop step 1's marker from ever lighting, so it is dropped rather than guessed at. Step 4 is demoted to medium: its ladder position is certain but neither the target name nor the zone is the page's -- the page writes only 'Naja' and never says where she stands, and 'Naja Salaheem' comes from the shipped index. It is kept because it is unambiguously the same NPC and resolves, but high was overstated.

notes:
Bullet 1 is one sentence that is really six fights in six different zones, and bullet 3 is the table that names them. One step per zone, all sharing a group, because the page says outright that any or all of them may already be dead before the quest is even taken -- there is no order to enforce, and a strict ladder would mark Abyssea - Tahrongi and nothing else.

Bullet 2 is NOT a step. It says the requirement is the TITLE from each NM, which no packet reports, and its sub-bullets are a way to CHECK: talking to the bard Zuah Lepahnyu in Port Jeuno (J-8) to read your titles back. Checking is not doing, and a marker on a Jeuno bard would be noise, so he is a note rather than a rung. That does mean the six fight steps are entirely unobservable.

EVIDENCE CAUTION. The Abyssite of discernment is also the header's Reward, which normally disqualifies it. It is used anyway, and flagged, because this quest does not END there: bullet 5 still has you enter the Hall of the Gods afterwards. Holding the abyssite therefore genuinely means 'the six are done, go to the Hall', which is the only advance this ladder can ever observe. The flag is deliberate so a human can overrule it.

The page never says where Joachim stands, so his step carries no zone rather than a guessed one. Bullet 5's 18:00-5:00 window is Vana'diel time, which the addon cannot see. Fame 'Abyssea' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

notes:
Five bullets and only two of them are steps. Bullet 3 is a note about repeat rewards; bullet 4 is the repeat rule; bullet 5 is the questline order. None is anything you do.

The header's 'Quest Reqs: Twitherym Wing x2' is the trade, not a prerequisite quest, so prev stays empty and the wings ride on the trade step as an AND-count of two. There is no obtain rung in front of it: a trade step already carries its own holding requirement, and an unmarkable 'go get wings' row between two visits to the same NPC would only split one marker into two.

The four sources under bullet 2 -- Auction House, Ceizak Battlegrounds (G-10), Yahse Hunting Grounds (I-8), Outer Ra'Kaznar map 1 (F/G-6) -- are advice about where to farm, not places the quest sends you, so they stay in the note.

Repeating requires finishing the whole three-quest chain (this, A Good Pair of Crocs, A Shot in the Dark) in order every time. Nothing in the packets expresses a repeat precondition on OTHER quests, so it is flagged and left as prose. Fame 'Adoulin' is not one of the nine regions and gates nothing.

notes:
Small and clean, and it fixes a real v1 error: v1 puts Amaura in zone 102, La Theine Plateau, when the quest is in Abyssea - La Theine, zone 132. Three steps, all three markable, all in one zone.

Bullets 2 and 3 are ONE step. Bullet 2 sends you to the Jagged Cliff and bullet 3 describes what happens once you are there -- the bungee mini-game, the 'NOW' prompt, three attempts. There is only one thing to click, so there is one rung, and the Sunbeam fragment it can yield is its evidence.

The fragment is an Item Req rather than a Reward, so it is legitimate evidence. It sits on step 2 where it is obtained and NOT on step 3, which would be a duplicate.

Step 3 is the one place the schema cannot say what the page says. You may return to Amaura WITHOUT the fragment and still finish, for 60 Cruor instead of 120. items therefore holds the fragment, because that is the intended path and the one worth marking readiness for, and items_partial records that an alternative exists which no list can express. The Hi-Reraiser caveat -- you must not already be holding one -- is the same shape and is left as prose.

The mini-game only works between 6:00 and 18:00 Vana'diel time, which the addon cannot see. 'Zoning is required to repeat this quest' is a cooldown, not a step. Fame 'alth' is an Abyssea zone code and gates nothing.

notes:
Three bullets, four steps, and a zone fix: v1 puts Prishe in zone 36, the Chains-of-Promathia Empyreal Paradox, when this quest lives in Abyssea - Empyreal Paradox, zone 255.

Bullet 1 spans two zones -- you click the Transcendental Radiance standing in Qufim Island (F-7) and you arrive in Abyssea - Empyreal Paradox -- so it is recorded in the zone where the clicking happens, with the destination in the note. The Crimson traverser stone is the page's own 'for a key item', obtained at that step, so it is that step's evidence.

There are TWO entities called Transcendental Radiance, one at each end, which is exactly why every step carries its own zone: without them the two rows would be indistinguishable and each would draw in both places.

Bullet 2 is two rungs. Its own sentence is the examining -- once for a cutscene, again to enter the battlefield -- and its six sub-bullets are all Shinryu tactics, which is where the fight itself is described; there is no top-level bullet for the fight at all. A verb-scanner would have produced six steps out of those sub-bullets.

Start is left as the header's Prishe. She is a real standing NPC in the Paradox and the quest's closing step, but she is NOT what bullet 1 sends you to, so the flag records that the start marker and step 1 are in different zones. This quest is handed to you by the previous mission's cutscene rather than by talking to anyone.

He absorbs damage with his wings up while readying a weaponskill or casting, Mighty Guard cuts physical and magical damage hard, Cosmic Breath is a cone with Plague and Attack Down, Gyre Charge is AoE with Paralyze, and his ordinary melee counts as weaponskills for the Red/Blue/Green staggers.

notes:
Red Mage artifact, nine bullets, ten steps, and the longest honest ladder in this batch: five zones, eight markable rungs and two evidence points. v1 collapses the whole thing into one Curilla talk carrying both Item Reqs, so the Antique Coin and the Nail Puller only light the marker if you hold both at once -- here each sits on the step that produces it and each is consumed by the step after, which is exactly the shape the ladder is for.

'Level: 50+ Red Mage' is both gates: level 50 AND jobs ['RDM']. 'Repeatable: af' means false. 'Quest Reqs: Ability to access Chateau d'Oraguille' has no slot in the schema and no observable predicate, so it is flagged and gates nothing.

Bullet 5 is two NPCs and therefore two steps. The page places Sharzalion at (K-6) in the Lion Springs Tavern and says only that Daggao is 'in the bar as well', so Daggao inherits (K-6) -- an inference, flagged, and the alternative was no grid at all.

Bullets 6, 7 and 8 are three separate interactions in one room and stay three rungs: examine the Oaken Box to spawn the Guardian Statue, kill it for the Nail Puller, trade the puller back to the SAME box. Two of the three mark the same object, which is one marker, and the fight between them is genuinely there.

The quest does not end on an NPC. Bullet 9 is a zone-entry cutscene into Northern San d'Oria that hands over the Warlock's Chapeau, so the last step is a travel with nobody to turn in to. Inventing a hand-in back at Curilla would be a wrong marker. The chapeau is the Reward and is not used as evidence.
